chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Regeneration occurs in ____.
solution: Regeneration is the ability to regrow lost body parts and reproduce from body fragments. It occurs in planaria (and hydra), which can regenerate a complete organism from a small body fragment. Amoeba, paramoecium and euglena reproduce mainly by binary fission, not by regeneration.

stem: Lactobacillus brevis gives us the beverage ____.
solution: The lactic acid bacterium Lactobacillus brevis is used in the fermentation of cocoa beans to obtain cocoa. Wine and cider are produced by yeast (Saccharomyces), so cocoa is the correct answer.

stem: A minor change that occurs due to a change in the position of any nucleotide is termed as ____.
solution: A change in the sequence or position of nucleotides in DNA is called a mutation. Mutations are a source of variation. Transcription and translation are steps of protein synthesis, not changes in the gene.

stem: The atomic power plant in Maharashtra is ____.
solution: Tarapur Atomic Power Station (Palghar district) is the nuclear/atomic power plant in Maharashtra. Chandrapur is a thermal power station and Koyana is a hydroelectric project.

stem: An example of phylum Arthropoda is ____.
solution: Scorpion belongs to phylum Arthropoda (jointed appendages, chitinous exoskeleton). Starfish is an echinoderm, earthworm is an annelid, and hydra belongs to phylum Coelenterata.

stem: Pick the odd man out: duckbill platypus, pomfret, lungfish, peripatus.
solution: Pomfret is the odd one out. Duckbill platypus (connecting link between reptiles and mammals), lungfish (connecting link between fishes and amphibians) and peripatus (connecting link between Annelida and Arthropoda) are all connecting links, whereas pomfret is an ordinary bony fish and not a connecting link.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Write the co-relation: Skin : Melanin :: Pancreas : ____
solution: Pancreas : Insulin. Just as the skin produces the pigment melanin, the pancreas (its endocrine islets of Langerhans) secretes the hormone insulin.

stem: State true or false: Production of various useful aquatic organisms with the help of water is called blue revolution.
solution: True. Blue revolution refers to the large-scale production of useful aquatic organisms (fish and other aquatic life) through aquaculture and fisheries.

stem: Write the full form of WHO.
solution: WHO stands for World Health Organization.
Male : (b) \(44 + XY\). A human male has 44 autosomes and the sex chromosomes XY, giving the chromosome constitution \(44 + XY\); a female is \(44 + XX\).

stem: Give scientific reason: Though a tortoise lives on land as well as in water, it cannot be included in class Amphibia.
solution: A tortoise is included in class Reptilia, not Amphibia, because its body is covered by a hard, dry, keratinised shell/scales (not moist glandular skin), it respires only through lungs at all stages (amphibians can respire through moist skin and larvae use gills), it lays shelled (cleidoic) eggs on land, and it has no aquatic larval stage. Merely living partly in water is not enough; these reptilian characters keep it out of Amphibia.

stem: Give scientific reason: Hydroelectric energy, solar energy and wind energy are called renewable energies.
solution: These sources are continuously and naturally replenished and are practically inexhaustible — flowing water, sunlight and wind are available again and again and are not used up permanently. Hence they can be used repeatedly without getting exhausted, so they are called renewable (non-conventional) energy sources. They are also clean and non-polluting, unlike fossil fuels which are limited and get exhausted.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Give scientific reason: We feel tired after exercise.
solution: During vigorous exercise the muscles need a lot of energy but the supply of oxygen becomes insufficient. So the muscle cells carry out anaerobic respiration (lactic acid fermentation), breaking down glucose incompletely into lactic acid. Accumulation of lactic acid in the muscles causes fatigue, cramps and pain, and hence we feel tired after exercise.

stem: Write four adverse effects of radiations on the human body.
solution: Adverse effects of radiations on the human body: (1) They damage living cells and tissues (radiation burns). (2) They cause mutations in DNA, leading to cancers such as blood cancer (leukaemia) and skin cancer. (3) They cause harmful genetic changes that can be passed on to the next generation (birth defects). (4) They lower immunity and can cause anaemia, sterility, hair loss and even death on high exposure.

stem: Redraw and complete the given chart of 'Factors affecting the Social Health' (four factors).
solution: Factors affecting the Social Health: (1) Economic condition / poverty, (2) Addiction (alcohol, tobacco, drugs), (3) Unemployment, (4) Stress / mental tension. (Other acceptable factors: crime, superstitions, communal disharmony, imbalanced sex ratio.)

stem: Write any four important facts which must be thought over while considering the scope of disaster.
solution: Facts to consider regarding the scope of a disaster: (1) The geographical area / extent of the region likely to be affected. (2) The size of the human population and the number of people affected. (3) The extent of damage to property, buildings, infrastructure and the environment. (4) The capacity of available resources and rescue/relief machinery to handle the situation. (Also: the duration and intensity of the disaster and the possibility of an epidemic afterwards.)

stem: Name two fuels obtained by microbial processes. Why is it necessary to increase the use of such fuels?
solution: Two fuels obtained by microbial processes are biogas (methane, produced by the action of methanogenic bacteria on organic waste) and ethanol / bio-ethanol (produced by fermentation of sugars by yeast). It is necessary to increase the use of such fuels because they are renewable and eco-friendly, they reduce dependence on limited fossil fuels (petroleum, coal), they cause less air pollution, and they help in the useful disposal of organic waste.

stem: What is DNA fingerprinting? Where is it mainly useful?
solution: DNA fingerprinting is a technique used to identify an individual on the basis of the unique pattern of specific nucleotide sequences in the DNA, which differs from person to person. It is mainly useful in forensic science for identifying criminals, in settling paternity/maternity and disputed-parentage cases, in identifying dead bodies in accidents/disasters, and in the study of genetic diseases and evolutionary relationships.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: (a) What are vitamins? (b) Classify them according to their solubility. (c) Give one example of each type as per the above classification.
solution: (a) Vitamins are complex organic micronutrients required by the body in very small quantities for growth, proper metabolism and protection against deficiency diseases. (b) According to solubility, vitamins are classified into two types: (i) fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) and (ii) water-soluble vitamins (B-complex and C). (c) Examples: fat-soluble — vitamin A (or D); water-soluble — vitamin C (or any B vitamin such as B1).

stem: Explain the term: Stem cells.
solution: Stem cells are unspecialised (undifferentiated) cells of the body that have the ability to divide repeatedly and to differentiate into various specialised types of cells and tissues. They are used in regenerative medicine and stem-cell therapy to repair or replace damaged tissues and organs.

stem: Explain the term: Cloning.
solution: Cloning is the technique of producing one or more genetically identical copies (clones) of a cell, tissue or complete organism from a single parent cell without fertilisation. The clones have exactly the same genetic constitution as the parent. Example: the cloned sheep 'Dolly'.

stem: Explain the term: Genetically modified crops.
solution: Genetically modified (GM) crops are crop plants whose genetic material (DNA) has been deliberately altered by genetic engineering — a desired gene from another organism is introduced into them — to obtain useful traits such as higher yield, better nutrition, and resistance to pests, diseases or drought. Example: Bt cotton, which contains a bacterial gene for pest resistance.

stem: Complete the given paragraph by filling the blank spaces from the options given in the bracket. [oxygen, pyridines, mechanical, \(CO_2\), petroleum, fatal, polyester, norcadia]  Spilling of ____ oil occurs in the ocean due to various reasons. This oil may prove ____ and toxic to aquatic organisms. It is not easy to remove the oil layer from the surface of water by ____ method. However, bacteria like Pseudomonas spp. and Alcanovorax borkumensis have the ability to destroy the ____ and other chemicals. Hence, these bacteria are used to clear the oil spills. These are called hydrocarbonoclastic bacteria (HCB). HCB decompose the hydrocarbons and bring about the reaction of carbon with ____ . ____ and water is formed in this process.
solution: The completed paragraph: Spilling of petroleum oil occurs in the ocean due to various reasons. This oil may prove fatal and toxic to aquatic organisms. It is not easy to remove the oil layer from the surface of water by mechanical method. However, bacteria like Pseudomonas spp. and Alcanovorax borkumensis have the ability to destroy the pyridines and other chemicals. HCB decompose the hydrocarbons and bring about the reaction of carbon with oxygen. \(CO_2\) and water is formed in this process. (Blanks in order: petroleum, fatal, mechanical, pyridines, oxygen, \(CO_2\); the words polyester and norcadia are not used.)

stem: Observe the given picture and answer the questions: (a) Identify the given diagram. (b) What is the source of energy in this project? (c) Why is this source supposed to be eco-friendly?
solution: (a) The diagram is a wind energy generator (windmill / wind turbine). (b) The source of energy is wind energy — the kinetic energy of blowing wind rotates the turbine blades, which drive a generator to produce electricity. (c) It is eco-friendly because wind is a renewable and inexhaustible source, its use produces no smoke, harmful gases or pollution, it does not consume fuel and it does not cause global warming.

stem: Complete the following chart of 'Hobbies helpful to overcome stress' (six hobbies).
solution: Hobbies helpful to overcome stress: (1) Reading books, (2) Listening to or playing music, (3) Gardening, (4) Painting / drawing, (5) Playing games / sports, (6) Dancing. (Other acceptable hobbies: singing, trekking, yoga/meditation, collecting stamps or coins.)

stem: Write the names of any six materials which are to be in the first aid box.
solution: Six materials in a first aid box: (1) Cotton (absorbent cotton wool), (2) Roller bandage, (3) Antiseptic solution/lotion (e.g. Dettol/Savlon) and tincture of iodine, (4) Adhesive tape and adhesive dressings/band-aid, (5) A pair of scissors, (6) A thermometer. (Other acceptable items: sterile gauze pieces, safety pins, tweezers/forceps, pain-relief balm, ORS packets.)

stem: (a) Define vestigial organs. (b) Write the names of any two vestigial organs in the human body. (c) Write the name of those animals in which these vestigial organs are functional.
solution: (a) Vestigial organs are reduced, non-functional (or poorly functional) organs in the body of an organism that were well developed and functional in its ancestors; they are anatomical evidence of evolution. (b) Two vestigial organs in humans: the vermiform appendix and the nictitating membrane (plica semilunaris) of the eye. (Also: muscles of the ear pinna, wisdom teeth, coccyx/tail bone.) (c) The appendix (a large functional caecum) is functional in herbivorous mammals such as rabbit and horse (helps in digestion of cellulose), and the nictitating membrane is functional in birds, reptiles and amphibians (e.g. frog).

stem: Calcareous spines are present on the body. Tube feet are used for locomotion and for capturing prey also. — Identify the phylum and give one example.
context: Read the statements and answer accordingly (identify the group and give one example):
solution: Phylum: Echinodermata. These animals have a spiny calcareous (spiny-skinned) body and tube feet (part of the water-vascular system) used for locomotion and capturing prey. Example: starfish (Asterias) [or sea urchin].

stem: I live in your small intestine. Pseudocoelom is present in my thread-like body. — Identify the phylum and give one example.
context: Read the statements and answer accordingly (identify the group and give one example):
solution: Phylum: Aschelminthes (Nematoda). These are thread-like (round) worms with a pseudocoelom (false body cavity); many are endoparasites of the small intestine. Example: Ascaris (roundworm) [or Enterobius, the pinworm].

stem: My body is spindle shaped. I respire with the help of gills. — Identify my class and give one example.
context: Read the statements and answer accordingly (identify the group and give one example):
solution: Class: Pisces (fishes). They have a streamlined, spindle-shaped body and respire with the help of gills. Example: Labeo (rohu) [or Scoliodon, or pomfret].

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: What is the work of the vas deferens?
context: Answer the following questions based on the human male reproductive system:
solution: The vas deferens (sperm duct) carries the mature sperms from the epididymis of the testis towards the urethra (via the seminal vesicle and ejaculatory duct) for release.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: By which type of cell division are sperms formed?
context: Answer the following questions based on the human male reproductive system:
solution: Sperms are formed by meiosis (meiotic cell division), which halves the chromosome number so that each sperm is haploid.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Name any two unpaired organs of the male reproductive system.
context: Answer the following questions based on the human male reproductive system:
solution: Two unpaired organs of the male reproductive system are the prostate gland and the penis (also the urethra). (The testes, epididymes, vasa deferentia and seminal vesicles are paired.)

stem: Complete the flow chart: Classification of threatened species (into four categories).
context: Answer the following questions based on environmental conservation and biodiversity:
solution: Classification of threatened species: (1) Extinct species, (2) Endangered species, (3) Vulnerable species, (4) Rare species.

stem: How can biodiversity be conserved? Give any four points.
context: Answer the following questions based on environmental conservation and biodiversity:
solution: Biodiversity can be conserved by: (1) In-situ conservation — protecting species in their natural habitats through national parks, sanctuaries and biosphere reserves. (2) Ex-situ conservation — protecting species outside their habitat in zoos, botanical gardens, gene banks and seed banks. (3) Preventing deforestation and habitat destruction and promoting afforestation. (4) Banning poaching and illegal trade of wild animals/plants and creating public awareness for conservation. (Also: controlling pollution and preventing over-exploitation of resources.)

stem: Complete the flow chart: Colour of the pages in the Red List of Endangered Species (Red List \(\rightarrow\) two colours).
solution: The Red List (Red Data Book) uses coloured pages: (1) Red colour pages — record the critically endangered / endangered species, and (2) Green colour pages — record the species that were once endangered but have now recovered (their population has been restored).
